text:
Sara: :rotating_light: seeing a flood of SLO burn alerts for prod-generation - burn-rate spiking across multiple windows. paging started for many routes. Not sure if this is real customer impact or noisy thresholds. Anyone oncall can triage?
MonitoringBot: [ALERT] prod-generation.slo.burn_rate high - windows=[1m,5m,15m] - current_burn=12.4x - pages=7 - triggered_at=2499998887
oncall-bot: Pager triggered: prod-generation - Severity: page - Escalation path: oncall -> eng-sre -> eng-runtime
Mike: I'm on it. Moving to channel. First, do we have traffic spike or error budget leak? Can someone paste top offending routes?
Devon: Looking at live tail - it's primarily /v1/generate and a handful of rerank calls. 503 rate up ~6% for the last 6m. No obvious deploys in last hour.
Sara: Customer impact: we are seeing some requests time out, some increased latency. Not global but multiple customers. Recommend temporary changes to alerting so we don't page for every short spike while we mitigate.
Mike: Agreed. Plan: 1) adjust paging criteria to only page on sustained multi-window burn or high 1m when accompanied by errors; 2) mute lower-severity duplicates; 3) create a dashboard for cross-window correlation.
Josh: Can we do step 1 quickly? How do we modify the rule?
Devon: In OpsAlert we can change the paging rule. Current rule snippet:```
alert prod_generation_slo_burn
if burn_rate > 3 for any window in [1m,5m,15m]
labels { severity = "page" }
```
Proposed temporary tweak:```
alert prod_generation_slo_burn
if (burn_rate > 5 and window == "1m") or (burn_rate > 2 and window in [5m,15m] for >= 2 consecutive windows)
labels { severity = "page" }
```
This reduces pages for short-lived 1m spikes.
Mike: That looks good. I'll apply a temporary rule and set an automatic rollback in 30m. Putting the change through now.
Mike: `opsctl alert update prod_generation_slo_burn --rule-file /tmp/temp-rule.yaml --expires 30m`
MonitoringBot: Rule update accepted by OpsAlert; temporary rule will expire in 30m (applied by Mike).
Sara: While Mike does that, I'll open a quick Grafana panel correlating 1m/5m/15m burn with 503 rate and CPU on the inference pool. I'll post link when ready.
Devon: Also recommend enabling dedupe on alert group key customer_id so we don't page for the same customer repeatedly. That reduces noise during a single-customer issue.
Mike: Enabled dedupe: `opsctl alert patch prod_generation_slo_burn --group-by customer_id` :white_check_mark:
Josh: Good. Any immediate mitigations for customers? Can we shift traffic away from affected pools?
Devon: We can scale up a standby Dedicated pool and shift low-priority traffic there, but needs a quick routing rule. I'll open a canary route to drain the overloaded instances.
Devon: `routerctl shift --from pool-a --to pool-standby --routes /v1/generate:10%`
Devon: Doing a gradual 10% shift now.
MonitoringBot: Routing change detected, shift 10% initiated by Devon.
Sara: Dashboard: https://grafana.internal/redwood/d/abc123/prod-slo-burn-triage - includes side-by-side windows and top routes.
Mike: After change, 1m burn dropped from 12x to 3.5x within 4m. 503 rate down to 2.1%. Looks like routing helped.
Sara: Great. Next: post-incident followups - we need to: 1) update paging runbook to include multi-window conditions, 2) add dedupe/grouping as default for SLO burn alerts, 3) evaluate whether our default windows are too short for bursty workloads.
Josh: I'll own the runbook update (assign to Josh) and draft wording for paging criteria. Target EOD today?
Josh: I'll have a PR by 18:00.
Mike: I'll file a monitoring ticket to change default alert templates to include group-by and to propose new multi-window thresholds. Ticket: MON-2499.
Devon: I'll follow up with a quant test on a replayed workload to see how different window sets affect sensitivity.
Sara: For handoff - I'm going offline in 15m. Mike, can you be the next primary oncall for followup?
Mike: Yep. I'll monitor and escalate if we see re-escalation. I'll also keep the temporary rule until the monitoring ticket lands a more permanent change.
oncall-bot: Handoff note: Sara -> Mike at 2499998930 - reason: triage in progress.
MonitoringBot: Alert resolved for prod-generation.slo.burn_rate - current_burn=1.1x - resolved_at=2499998945
Sara: :thumbsup: thanks team. I'll create the incident doc and link it to MON-2499.
Mike: Summary actions: - Temporary rule applied (expires in 30m) - Dedupe enabled by customer_id - Routing 10% to standby - Dashboard created - Runbook PR (Josh) - Monitoring ticket MON-2499 (Mike)
Josh: Will add remediation notes in the PR and suggest default values for windowed thresholds.
Devon: Postmortem planned. I'll attach the replay tests.
Sara: Closing thread for now; if anything new pops up ping me DM. :white_check_mark:
